BODY
The account is strongest exactly where it grounds itself: c1 and c2 are earned by the material, c3 is honestly flagged as conjecture, and o1 is a real self-criticism rather than decoration. My objections are therefore not to the core diagnosis but to its order, one hidden disjunction, one internal tension, one overconfidence, and one omission — and I note where I may be mistaking the situation.

**1. The plan's order works against its own diagnosis.** The account closes by saying two unknowns determine whether this is a logistics problem or a relationship problem in a logistics costume — then schedules the logistics interventions (a)–(c) ahead of the only step, (d), that could answer the most important unknown. On two of the branches the account itself names (feeling out-voted; a process perceived as rigged), a system-design meeting that the avoidant friend skips, followed by a written system built in their absence, does not merely fail to help — it manufactures fresh evidence for the grievance. Reversing (d) and (a) costs almost nothing; the current order is expensive exactly on the branches where diagnosis matters most. Relatedly, u1 proposes carrying p1 as a question 'to answer there' — at the meeting — but on those branches the meeting is the one venue where an out-voted friend will not say so. Only the private conversation can bear that weight, which is a second reason it should come first.

**2. a3 hides a non-equivalence.** 'Weekly re-deal or trigger-based rules' is offered as an interchangeable either/or. The two differ in precisely the risk that matters here. With shifting schedules, 'first one home starts dinner' will in many weeks systematically load the same person — whoever's job ends earliest — converting a contested fairness question into a rules-legitimated structural one, with marginal incentives to dawdle and, in a household already disputing what agreements meant, a fresh contestable fact (who arrived home when). The weekly re-deal keeps drift visible and correctable; triggers automate the drift. If triggers are used at all, they need rotation or caps, and the account does not say so.

**3. a2 and o1 pull apart with no meeting point.** The remedy direction is checkable specificity; the self-caution's guard is minimality and revisability. Those are opposite pulls, and the account gives no criterion for where they meet. Worst, they diverge most on the account's own re-litigation branch, where a regretful or gaming reader exploits exactly the gaps a minimal record leaves. 'Written specificity helps in both cases' is asserted rather than shown. A repair sits unused inside the account's own materials: designate the weekly re-deal as the standing venue where wording disputes get settled, so the record needn't be courtroom-grade and o1's guard becomes workable rather than a hope.

**4. One piece of folk psychology is asserted past its evidence.** 'Avoidant people often engage readily in writing' may be true but has no support in the exposed material, and the async channel is double-edged: it can lower the cost of avoidance (skim, never reply — with the record then documenting the silence) as easily as the cost of engagement. a4's private conversation also carries an unflagged meta-risk: to someone avoiding chore-talks, a one-on-one about why they avoid chore-talks is still a chore-talk at one remove, and who delivers it matters if the out-voted branch is live. None of this kills a4; it counsels holding it loosely and pre-planning for non-response, which the account does not do.

**5. The plan has no floor.** Every remedy except (d) requires the participation whose absence is one of the presented problems. If the friend will not attend the meeting or reply to the note, the account has nothing in hand. A structural fallback exists and is partly unilateral: shrink the commons. Own dishes and own kit, personal zones, each person permanently owning one domain instead of rotating through all — each reduces the number of agreements the flat needs at all, and so reduces its exposure to later disputes about what any agreement meant. It is compatible with everything the account proposes and deserves a place as the plan's minimum rather than appearing nowhere.

Where I may be wrong: the material never says the user doesn't already know why the friend avoids the talks; if they do, objection 1 mostly dissolves into a shift of emphasis. Triggers may suit this particular flat's rhythm. And because the account hedges in the right places, some of my corrections are reweightings rather than found errors. Even so, the reordering in objection 1 is nearly free to adopt and costly to be wrong about, which makes it the one I would press.
COMMITMENTS

The selected account (h005.fork5.p.rival.0) poses this as a systems problem: agreements under-specified, an allocation mechanism mismatched to the schedules, participation made costly. Its own aside — that meaning-disputes may be re-litigation of deals someone regrets — gestures at a different diagnosis. This rival promotes that aside to the main claim: the household may have a ledger problem, not a specification problem.

A robust behavioural finding: when members of a couple estimate their own contributions to shared chores, the two sets of estimates sum to well over 100 percent. Both parties are honest; each remembers their own labour vividly and the other's dimly. Scale that to three flatmates, and the recurring 'we agreed this' / 'no we didn't' reads less like ambiguity in words and more like three private tallies colliding. 'That is not what I agreed to' is ledger-talk wearing contract-talk. Clarity helps, but disputes will not go to zero under any wording, so the design goal inverts: not unambiguous agreements, but cheap, bounded disagreements.

The avoidance also rereads. The other account treats it primarily as process-fatigue. Treat it instead as a predicted defeat: if the talks reliably end with the same person assigned, outvoted, or audited, then skipping them is rational behaviour from a permanent minority. The material cannot show whether the asker and the second friend function as a de facto bloc, but checking that privately comes before any redesign, because every mechanism fails in a household one member experiences as a tribunal. And a note on the asker's own position: whoever convenes the fix is doing a fourth chore — the coordination labour itself. Become permanent house manager and the avoider may end up avoiding you, not the chores.

Rival mechanisms, chosen to shrink the stakes rather than perfect the terms:

1. Rotating proposer/veto, replacing consensus. Each week one flatmate (rotating; deliberately include the avoider early) drafts the week's allocation in writing against the actual rosters. The others may veto the whole draft, not amend it line by line; a veto triggers a dull published fallback, e.g. last week's rota repeats. Hour-long negotiation becomes yes/no; the avoider gets turns holding the pen instead of the blame; the written record — the one element of the other account kept wholesale — survives as the proposer's draft.

2. A deliberately low house standard. Agree the standard all three actually accept, and make that the whole standard. Whatever anyone wants beyond it belongs to them — their labour or their money, never conscription by taste. Much chore warfare is the highest-standards flatmate taxing the rest; this untaxes them, and it licenses saying aloud that the flat will run below someone's preference on purpose.

3. A bounded dispute protocol. Every 'that is not what we agreed' gets exactly one airing at a fixed ten-minute weekly slot. Unresolved in one round, it is settled by alternation — whoever lost the last dispute wins this one — and never reopened. The crudeness is the feature: re-litigating wording must cost more than yielding.

4. A standing priced exit. Obtain one cleaner quote and leave it permanently on the table: any chore still contested after two cycles gets outsourced, cost split. Often the visible price of conflict ends it; when not, the most-contested items (bathroom, floors) leave the ledger entirely. A heavier variant, if veto rates run high: whole-domain ownership with quarterly rotation, each owner sovereign over methods and standards in their domain.

Order of operations, which is where this most differs from the selected account: first, private diagnostics, not a meeting — ask each friend separately what a fair week looks like, and ask the avoider outright whether the talks feel fair and whether they have real say; compare the three answers before proposing anything. Second, offer mechanisms 1–4 as a menu and let the avoider choose; the choosing is the re-engagement. Third, run a four-week trial with an explicit expiry — a lease, not a constitution. Fourth, if the avoider will not engage with even the mechanism they selected, stop treating this as chores: the question has become whether the household still works, and that conversation is better had now than after six more months of crockery-based trench warfare.

Objections to my own posing: priced mechanisms assume flatmates who read chores as allocations; those who read them as care will experience a cleaner quote, ill-timed, as an insult. The ledger diagnosis is as speculative from outside as the specification diagnosis; the two are empirically distinguishable only by watching whether clear written terms actually cut dispute frequency — the trial is the assay, not the theory. And if both diagnoses keep failing, the residue is that the fights are proxy for something between particular people, in which case the friend who walked away from the talks is the only reliable informant left.

The chore fights look like three separate faults stacked on top of each other, and it helps to keep them apart.

**1. Agreements that aren't really agreements.** 'We agree on who will do something, but later disagree about what the agreement meant' is the signature of under-specified commitments — no settled what, when, or what-done-looks-like. Three people can leave the same conversation holding three different agreements, each honestly believed. The remedy is boring but effective: agreements get written down somewhere all three can see, in checkable terms ('kitchen counters wiped and dishwasher started by 9pm'), not in good-intention terms.

**2. An allocation that can't survive the schedules.** A fixed rota assumes stable weeks. With shifting work schedules, any static division decays within a fortnight, and every failure reopens negotiation at the worst moment — at the scene of an unwashed pan. Two robust alternatives: a short weekly re-deal (ten minutes, same time each week, allocate the coming week against actual schedules), or trigger-based rules ('first one home starts dinner'). Either moves renegotiation out of the moment of failure.

**3. A participant opting out — and this one matters most.** One friend avoiding the conversations means the conversation itself has become a cost. The material doesn't say why: conflict-aversion, feeling out-voted two-against-one, a sense the process is rigged, or something unrelated that the chore talks have become a proxy for. What I'd try: approach them one-on-one, not about any specific chore, ask what would make the household talks easier, and offer an asynchronous channel (the shared written record doubles as this) — avoidant people often engage readily in writing.

Conjectures I'm holding loosely: the disagreement about meaning may sometimes be re-litigation — someone reopening a deal they regret — rather than genuine ambiguity; written specificity helps in both cases, so it doesn't change the advice. The avoidance may also be an early symptom of someone drifting toward moving out; worth bearing in mind, not worth acting on preemptively.

What I'd actually do, in order: (a) propose one short meeting framed explicitly as fixing the system, not reviewing who failed last week; (b) there, agree a short list of standards and pick one allocation mechanism from point 2; (c) set up the written record in the group chat or on the fridge; (d) separately and privately, have the one-on-one conversation with the avoidant friend; (e) after two or three weekly cycles, revisit whatever keeps failing rather than treating any arrangement as final.

One caution against my own remedy: a written chore system can curdle into bureaucracy and relocate the fight from the sink to the wording of the list. Guard against it by keeping the record minimal and treating it as revisable, not law.

Unanswered: whether the three of you actually share minimum standards (a standards gap needs negotiation of the standards themselves, possibly with trades across domains), and what the avoidant friend is really avoiding. Those two unknowns determine whether this is a logistics problem or a relationship problem wearing a logistics costume.",

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[96632772dc15b6e3] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/response; selected view: both
Artifact: e80f5b9e5e90f73fb671e10d12f00705ee67715f6d83f04f77fb8412ce39ea93
Original body SHA256: f2cdafcc4fc3b3af11f99e5e4925759db92e2589fb71ab114051cf9641e10531

Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
Read together, the criticism and the rival converge on the same correction from different directions, and that convergence is the strongest result available. Neither engages the other; each derives 'diagnose privately before designing publicly' on its own grounds — the criticism from branch analysis (on the out-voted and rigged-process branches, a design meeting the avoider skips manufactures fresh evidence for the grievance), the rival from the standing-defeat reading (attendance as predictable loss). I adopt it, and the grounds are stronger than a preference: reversing the order is nearly free because a private conversation obliges nobody, while a meeting commits all three — an asymmetric bet worth taking at moderate confidence. The companion correction (ob2) follows: p1 is not answerable at the meeting and stops being carried as a meeting question.

The private round uses the rival's questions rather than the account's: 'what does a fair week look like' and 'do the talks feel fair, do you have a real say' are better built against the criticism's meta-risk — asking someone why they avoid chore-talks is still a chore-talk at one remove, while asking what fairness looks like is not. Two precautions are taken from the edges of both pieces: run the same questions with both friends and tell each that you are (the rival's own r14 worry about coalition-appearance dissolves only if the symmetry is visible), and plan for silence in advance (ob5) — silence routes to the floor below, not to a repeat attempt. One self-directed addition: the ledger mechanism applies to the asker too. Walk in assuming your own tally is inflated; it turns the round from audit into listening.

The design goal is revised, not just the order. The rival's ledger claim rests on a real, commonly cited result — partners' estimates of their own shares of household work sum to well past 100 percent — whose exact size is unverifiable here, but nothing below needs the number; the mechanism (each person remembers their own labour vividly) is plausible on its face and predicts the asker's perceptions as much as the friends'. Under-specification (c1) and ledger divergence (r1) are co-possible, and the exposed material cannot choose between them — but they respond differently to written clarity, so the trial with written terms plus a bounded dispute protocol is the discriminator. And because ledger divergence survives clarity, disputes will not reach zero: the goal becomes disagreements that are cheap to finish. That single revision also dissolves the tension the criticism found between checkable specificity (a2) and minimal revisability (o1): if every wording dispute gets exactly one airing at the weekly slot, then settlement by alternation and a bar on reopening, the record's completeness stops being load-bearing and it can afford to be minimal. Two criticisms meeting at one mechanism; take both.

On allocation: ob3 is adopted and the account's either/or rejected as presented — uncapped triggers load the early-home person systematically and mint a new contestable fact in a household that litigates facts. Triggers survive only capped or rotated, and only if the flat actively wants fewer decisions. In place of the plain re-deal I take the rival's rotating proposer/veto: same weekly cadence against actual rosters, but rotation puts the pen in the avoider's hand early, the whole-draft-only veto keeps the meeting at yes/no, and a published default makes a veto cheap. This also answers r4, the one claim here that neither earlier piece contained: convening is a fourth chore, and if the asker becomes permanent house manager the role itself becomes the thing avoided. Rotating authorship is the countermeasure — and since the task is asker-posed, the risk is live by construction.

Standards: r7 converts the account's open p2 into a rule — the house standard is the highest standard all three actually accept, and anything above it belongs to whoever wants it, their labour or their money. It subsumes a5's standards negotiation for the common case; a5's cross-domain trades remain for the case where no common floor exists. The gate matters: 'all three accept' presupposes the avoider's answer from the private round — one more reason design waits. Priced exit: adopted as an option, not a fixture, on the rival's own demotion (chores read as care, not allocation) plus an unknown the material does not settle, comparable budgets. Get the quote, leave it visible, decide items and splits only with prior agreement.

Floor: ob6 is adopted and promoted from fallback to fixture — own dishes and kit, personal zones, permanent single-owner domains (convergent with the rival's r12). Every other remedy presupposes the participation whose absence is itself a symptom; this one is partly unilateral and removes agreements instead of administering them. It runs in parallel from the start, not after failure.

Assembled order: (1) the private round as above; (2) one short meeting framed as fixing the system, mechanisms offered as a menu with the avoider choosing first — the choosing is part of the re-engagement, not a courtesy; (3) a four-week trial with explicit expiry, the dispute protocol running, the record minimal; (4) the floor operating throughout; (5) the rival's r15 branch held in reserve: if the avoider will not engage even with a mechanism they chose, or the round shows the disengagement predates the chores, the question stops being chores, and that conversation is cheaper now than later.

Left open deliberately: whether the asker already knows what the avoider is avoiding (the criticism's pr1 — if so, step 1 is confirmation, not discovery); who should deliver the private round if a two-against-one perception is live; whether alternation should be tallied per person or per pair among three (default per person, untested here); and the actual standards gap, which only the round reveals. If both diagnoses fail in trial, the residue points between particular people, and the friend who left the talks is the only reliable informant — which is where this plan starts.

  "body": "Read together, the criticism and the rival converge on the same correction from different directions, and that convergence is the strongest result available. Neither engages the other; each derives 'diagnose privately before designing publicly' on its own grounds — the criticism from branch analysis (on the out-voted and rigged-process branches, a design meeting the avoider skips manufactures fresh evidence for the grievance), the rival from the standing-defeat reading (attendance as predictable loss). I adopt it, and the grounds are stronger than a preference: reversing the order is nearly free because a private conversation obliges nobody, while a meeting commits all three — an asymmetric bet worth taking at moderate confidence. The companion correction (ob2) follows: p1 is not answerable at the meeting and stops being carried as a meeting question.\n\nThe private round uses the rival's questions rather than the account's: 'what does a fair week look like' and 'do the talks feel fair, do you have a real say' are better built against the criticism's meta-risk — asking someone why they avoid chore-talks is still a chore-talk at one remove, while asking what fairness looks like is not. Two precautions are taken from the edges of both pieces: run the same questions with both friends and tell each that you are (the rival's own r14 worry about coalition-appearance dissolves only if the symmetry is visible), and plan for silence in advance (ob5) — silence routes to the floor below, not to a repeat attempt. One self-directed addition: the ledger mechanism applies to the asker too. Walk in assuming your own tally is inflated; it turns the round from audit into listening.\n\nThe design goal is revised, not just the order. The rival's ledger claim rests on a real, commonly cited result — partners' estimates of their own shares of household work sum to well past 100 percent — whose exact size is unverifiable here, but nothing below needs the number; the mechanism (each person remembers their own labour vividly) is plausible on its face and predicts the asker's perceptions as much as the friends'. Under-specification (c1) and ledger divergence (r1) are co-possible, and the exposed material cannot choose between them — but they respond differently to written clarity, so the trial with written terms plus a bounded dispute protocol is the discriminator. And because ledger divergence survives clarity, disputes will not reach zero: the goal becomes disagreements that are cheap to finish. That single revision also dissolves the tension the criticism found between checkable specificity (a2) and minimal revisability (o1): if every wording dispute gets exactly one airing at the weekly slot, then settlement by alternation and a bar on reopening, the record's completeness stops being load-bearing and it can afford to be minimal. Two criticisms meeting at one mechanism; take both.\n\nOn allocation: ob3 is adopted and the account's either/or rejected as presented — uncapped triggers load the early-home person systematically and mint a new contestable fact in a household that litigates facts. Triggers survive only capped or rotated, and only if the flat actively wants fewer decisions. In place of the plain re-deal I take the rival's rotating proposer/veto: same weekly cadence against actual rosters, but rotation puts the pen in the avoider's hand early, the whole-draft-only veto keeps the meeting at yes/no, and a published default makes a veto cheap. This also answers r4, the one claim here that neither earlier piece contained: convening is a fourth chore, and if the asker becomes permanent house manager the role itself becomes the thing avoided. Rotating authorship is the countermeasure — and since the task is asker-posed, the risk is live by construction.\n\nStandards: r7 converts the account's open p2 into a rule — the house standard is the highest standard all three actually accept, and anything above it belongs to whoever wants it, their labour or their money. It subsumes a5's standards negotiation for the common case; a5's cross-domain trades remain for the case where no common floor exists. The gate matters: 'all three accept' presupposes the avoider's answer from the private round — one more reason design waits. Priced exit: adopted as an option, not a fixture, on the rival's own demotion (chores read as care, not allocation) plus an unknown the material does not settle, comparable budgets. Get the quote, leave it visible, decide items and splits only with prior agreement.\n\nFloor: ob6 is adopted and promoted from fallback to fixture — own dishes and kit, personal zones, permanent single-owner domains (convergent with the rival's r12). Every other remedy presupposes the participation whose absence is itself a symptom; this one is partly unilateral and removes agreements instead of administering them.   "body": "This invocation exposes the synthesis response, the earlier account's commitments, and the objection set; the origin slot is absent. A coverage check shows the synthesis already sits downstream of both exposed inputs: every record of the account and the objection is adopted, revised, or dissolved inside it, with one silent drop (the async channel) that this carry makes explicit. The carry's job is therefore consolidation and status annotation, not redesign — keeping the synthesis as the standing account while pinning down what its parts now are.\n\nWhat is retained, with grounds attached. The sequencing fix (private round before design meeting) rests on two independent derivations plus a cost asymmetry, and the redundancy is itself the ground: a later criticism has to beat both derivations, not one. The remedy set is diagnosis-agnostic — under-specification and ledger divergence receive the same written clarity, bounded disputes, and floor — so the four-week trial assays expectations and the success metric, not the remedies; the trial can fail to discriminate without invalidating any step, and only the reading of the dispute rate and the trigger for the terminal branch depend on its outcome. The dissolution of the specificity-versus-minimality tension via a bounded dispute venue is the load-bearing move that lets the record stay minimal; it should not be re-separated. Rotation (of both proposal authorship and the convening role) is what answers the fourth-chore problem, and the floor plus terminal branch are the only elements that survive total non-participation — that spine is participation-independent by construction, which is precisely why it stays.\n\nStatus changes recorded. The account's core diagnosis is demoted from diagnosis-in-hand to one of two co-possible hypotheses; the objection set's claim that it 'survives' remains true, but only in that weaker sense, since nothing exposed can choose between the two readings and the trial is the discriminator. The async written channel, half of the account's private-conversation step, was dropped without remark in the synthesis; this carry withdraws it as a default step on the objection's double-edge grounds (it can document silence as easily as engagement) while leaving it available as something the avoider could themselves choose from the menu. Triggers, p1-in-plenary, and the zero-disputes criterion stay rejected; the standards question stays answered by the gated common-floor rule.\n\nThe one defect this pass finds in the synthesis is internal: the design meeting lets the avoider choose first and runs whatever is chosen, yet the surrounding commitments specify the allocation, record, standards, outsourcing, and floor designs unconditionally. Either the choice is real and those designs are displaceable defaults, or they are fixed and the choosing is performative — and a detected performative choice corroborates exactly the rigged-process grievance the sequencing was rebuilt to avoid. The repair is an annotation, not a redesign: before the meeting, mark which elements are displaceable by the avoider's choice (the mechanism designs) and which are fixed invariants (trial expiry, the bounded dispute rule, the floor, the terminal branch).\n\nOpen problems carried unchanged: who delivers the private round if a two-against-one perception is live; the tally rule for three-party alternation (default per person, untested); whether the asker already knows what the avoider is avoiding — the absent origin settles nothing here and must not be read as evidence either way — and the qualitative-only status of the ledger finding. Proposed uptake for the next complete invocation: the synthesis commitment set as the operative plan, its claims and objections as grounds and constraints, the status annotation applied before any meeting is convened, and the four problems attached. Nothing in this carry requires discarding anything from the synthesis.",
